recipes.title: Thomas Keller’s Butternut Soup with Brown Butter, Sage and Nutmeg Crème Fraîche
recipes.notes: A silky squash soup finished with nutty brown butter. It can be made a day ahead; brown the butter just before serving.

ingredients.name: Sage
ingredients.prep: plus a few leaves to garnish (optional)

ingredients.name: Leek
ingredients.prep: sliced, white and light green parts

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and line a small tray. Cut the squash where the neck meets the round base. Halve the base, scoop out the seeds, rub with a little of the oil, season, tuck a sage sprig into each half and roast cut side down for about an hour, until completely soft. Scoop out the flesh.
While it roasts, peel the neck and cut it into ½-inch cubes (about 4 cups). Tie the thyme, parsley and bay leaves into a small bundle with a few peppercorns.
Warm the rest of the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Cook the leek, carrot, shallot and onion, stirring often, for about 6 minutes, until soft but not browned.
Add the cubed squash, garlic, 1½ teaspoons salt and ½ teaspoon pepper and cook gently for 3 minutes, without letting anything colour. Stir in the honey and cook 2 to 3 minutes more.
Pour in the stock, add the herb bundle and simmer until the squash is tender, 10 to 15 minutes. Add the roasted squash and simmer gently for 30 minutes.
Take out the herbs. Blend the soup in batches until very smooth, then press it through a fine sieve. Taste for salt and pepper. It keeps well in the fridge overnight.
Whisk the crème fraîche with a pinch of nutmeg until it just holds its shape. Keep it cold.

Reheat the soup, adding a splash of stock if it’s thick. In a very hot skillet, cook the butter until it foams, then turns hazelnut brown and smells nutty, and pour it straight into the soup. Watch it: it goes from brown to burnt in seconds.
If you like, fry a few sage leaves in a thin layer of hot oil for 30 to 45 seconds until crisp, then drain and salt them.
Serve each bowl with a spoonful of the nutmeg crème fraîche, black pepper, sage leaves or chives, and a little olive oil.

recipes.title: Bloody Mary Tomato Salad
recipes.notes: Everything good about a Bloody Mary, as a salad. Best with ripe summer tomatoes.

ingredients.name: Tomatoes
ingredients.prep: ripe, any kind, cut into 1- to 2-inch pieces

steps: Toss the celery and red onion with the lemon juice, sugar and ¼ teaspoon salt. Leave them to soften for 5 to 10 minutes.
Stir together the soy sauce, balsamic, hot sauce, grated garlic, celery salt and olive oil.
Drain the celery and onion and squeeze out any extra liquid.
Put the tomatoes in a big bowl with the celery and onion, add the dressing and the pepper and fold gently. Taste for salt, and finish with parsley.

recipes.title: Banana Bread
recipes.notes: One bowl, no mixer. Swap the walnuts for pecans, chocolate chips or raisins.

ingredients.name: Butter
ingredients.prep: melted, or vegetable oil, plus more for the pan

ingredients.name: Walnuts
ingredients.prep: chopped, plus 2 tbsp for the top

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease an 8×4 or 9×5-inch loaf pan.
In a large bowl, whisk the mashed banana with the sugar, melted butter, eggs and vanilla.
In another bowl, whisk the flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Stir the dry mix into the wet just until no flour shows, then fold in the ½ cup walnuts.
Spread the batter in the pan and scatter the last 2 tablespoons of walnuts on top.
Bake 50 to 60 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Check at 40 minutes and lay foil over the top if it’s already deep golden.

recipes.title: Chicken with Braised Cherry Tomatoes and Burrata
recipes.notes: A one-pan weeknight dinner. Good with a big salad and crusty bread.
steps: Season the chicken with 1 teaspoon each of salt and pepper and a good shake of paprika. Heat the oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken 5 to 7 minutes per side, until cooked through (165°F inside). Move it to a plate.
Turn the heat down, add the garlic and cook for a minute. Pour in ¼ cup water and scrape up the browned bits; let it bubble for a minute.
Add the tomatoes, the rest of the salt and pepper, a pinch of red pepper flakes, the balsamic, honey and thyme. Cover and simmer 10 minutes, until the tomatoes slump.
Slice the chicken, slide it back into the pan and warm it through, uncovered, for 1 to 2 minutes.
Tear the burrata over the top, turn off the heat and let it sit for 3 minutes. Finish with black pepper, red pepper flakes and toasted pine nuts.
